sections.html: Markiana nigripinnis is one of the most unusual tetras. It grows to a common size of 12 cm, rarely 15 cm total length. It is easy to keep.
The species inhabits the river basins of the Paraná, Paraguay and the Marmoré (Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay). The specimens imported originate from Argentina.
As it is a relatively large and lively fish that must be kept in schools, one should have a large tank to keep them.

Due to the southern subtropical region where the fish occurs it is not necessary to install a heater in the tank. During summertime the fish can be kept even in garden ponds. Water conditions are of no great importance.
It is an omnivorous species that needs to be fed with plant material, too.
It must be kept in schools. As M. nigripinnis is a hardy and not shy species, it is an ideal companion for large cichlids like Geophagus brasiliensis, for example.
There are specimens with deep orange, black bordered anal fins (males?) and specimens with light orange anal fins without a black border (females?).

The body colour is blue-green-metallic-silvery, with a black spot on the base of the caudal fin; a humeral spot is present, but not always visible. Along the horizontal scale rows are black zigzag lines. The most obvious feature is the very long anal fin, which has a brilliant orange colour. Specimens brought in in autumn show extraordinary brilliant colours.

photos.author: Florencia Brancolini, Priscilla Minotti, Lucila Protogino, Hugo López, and Claudio Baigún
